evidence: The frozen workbook row and skill quality-checks.md:142-143 require the judge to be told to exercise interaction/time/viewport behavior rather than judge first paint. This source-level requirement is satisfied. Frozen task instruction.md:5 expressly requests a desktop workspace and excludes theme switching and a special phone layout; hireops_rules.md:59-67 fixes the stored reference moment, so real-clock waiting or clock advancement is not a requirement. Functional prompt.md:9,15,17 requires ordinary UI creation and fresh independent-context retrieval, and restricts replays to actual observed request shapes. Its P4 (lines29-35) performs approval, two revisions and rescission through the UI; B1/B2/B4/B6 (lines53-65) performs preview/commit, state-changing stale controls, simultaneous requests, and original-result UI retry after later actions. P10 line49 requires an actual restart followed by readback and retry. Polish judge.toml:23,32,41,50 requires changing/submitting retained form values, a successful correction, a real request interruption, stale refusal/recovery, and a forwarded successful commit whose response delivery is suppressed before a same-operation UI retry. Thus snapshots alone cannot establish the interactive criteria. Visual prompt.md:10 requires traversal of all six product views and harmless detail/form surfaces at a conventional desktop viewport; visual criteria concern desktop craft, with no responsive/theme criterion silently graded at initial paint. Corroborating raw evidence: local/batch-ui/results.json reports successful labelled editor/preview/UI commit, stale refusal preserving selected terms followed by new-key correction, and exactly one forwarded real commit response (HTTP200) suppressed before UI retry; local/legacy-ui/results.json records UI create/approve/revise/rescind and one aborted rescission request followed by retained-date retry. I read both drivers: they click/fill/select, wait for actual rendered outcomes, and inspect resulting product state. Their source hashes match all 14 and 13 corresponding frozen solution files, respectively. Independently recomputed all 292 current raw-index artifact hashes with no mismatch; verification and exact cited artifact hashes are preserved in per-row-review/evidence/34/hash-verification.json (index SHA256 1ef29f836bb775ef2ed19fc158bee979aef4d43ead0578fdb13fe9bacb6daad1). These are finite scripted golden observations, not execution of the configured LLM judges, full workload measurements, Oracle/model scores or portal clearance. No such claim supports this row verdict; this row passes the explicit source-directed exercise standard. The separate required configured-runtime evidence remains unmeasured in the index.
counterexample: Broken-app challenge: a polished seeded workspace with working basic requisition creation but inert coordinated commit controls could look convincing on first paint and satisfy the small backend gate. It cannot earn the coordinated interaction outcomes because Functional B1 requires UI commit plus newly persisted successors/settlements, and Polish requires a successful commit control and a real lost-response retry. Likewise clearing an editor after refusal is exposed by Polish's changed valid field plus invalid field/correction sequence. No row-34 false pass found. Conforming-alternative challenge: a single-theme desktop-only app with different navigation labels, inline forms instead of modals, generated IDs, semantic date displays and read-only retained-date Retry confirmation is accepted: instruction.md:5, functional prompt.md:13 and polish judge.toml:32 expressly permit these choices. No hidden phone resize, theme toggle, animation timing, exact-label or modal demand found.
